$comment: 'merge' adds a key ONLY when absent (non-destructive, safe to re-run).
'set' forces a value every run - use only for values the deployer owns.
$preserveNote: robocopy /MIR DELETES destination files absent from the publish source. Everything here is host-local STATE, not a deliverable: omitting impact-*.db once destroyed 344 KB of ranker learning data on jvgr22. '*.bak-*' covers config backups taken by ANY tool, not just this script - Invoke-NodeCleanup.ps1 writes them too and one was deleted by /MIR seconds after being taken. WatchList.xml and Prepare-Agent.bat are controller-only and are never expected on an agent. SQLITE WAL: orchestrator.db / impact-*.db are listed WITH their -wal and -shm siblings on purpose - SQLite keeps committed data in -wal until a checkpoint, so copying or preserving the .db alone yields a stale or unusable database. Any script that file-copies one of these must take all three together, or stop the controller first. The four native .dll entries (libSkiaSharp, libHarfBuzzSharp, e_sqlite3, LdaNative) sit at the deployed ROOT but ship in the payload only under runtimes\win-x64\native\, so /MIR would delete the root copies the app may load from; all four were verified byte-identical to the payload build before being listed. Measured 2026-10-03: e_sqlite3 actually loads from runtimes\win-x64\native\, so the root copies are vestigial and these four entries can be dropped once a report render and an Impact ranking confirm the same for Skia/HarfBuzz/Lda. _patchbackup and _dllbackup are rollback sets managed by Invoke-NodeCleanup.ps1 BackupFolders retention. Verify with: compare the deployed folder against publish\controller and add anything that is not a build artifact.

controllerConfigPatch.$note: 'merge' adds a key only when absent, so a re-deploy never overwrites operator-tuned values and never touches server-specific settings such as VocabularyFile.
